title: Open direct-image finiteness over a regular base of dimension at most one
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme] with Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in every local ring of $S$, put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $T\to S$ be separated of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For any open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and any constructible sheaf $F$ of modules over the constant sheaf $A_V$ on the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], every higher direct image $R^qj_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $q\geq0$, is a constructible $A_T$-module sheaf, and there is an integer $c_F\geq0$ such that $R^qj_*F=0$ for $q>c_F$. The bound may depend on $F$; no bound for arbitrary nonconstructible sheaves is asserted. No excellence, dualizing-complex, or purity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), printed p.197, for dimension-one bases, applied to f=j and n=ell. Dimension-zero bases are covered by replacing S by the disjoint union S ⊔ Spec Q[t], of dimension one, and using the same j. Also stated directly for the regular dimension-at-most-one case by Zheng, literature/zheng-six-operations-lefschetz-verdier-DM-stacks_arXiv-1006.3810.pdf, Proposition 3.16(1), printed p.19, before Construction 3.17.

proof.text: First $T$ is Noetherian since it is of finite type over $S$. Every open of $T$ is quasi-compact, so $j$ is quasi-compact and of finite type; in particular its higher direct images admit the strict-local stalk formula. Regularity makes $S$ normal, and its finitely many irreducible components are disjoint open integral schemes. Work on each component and combine the resulting finite stratifications and vanishing bounds at the end. Open restriction commutes with $Rj_*$. The empty base has empty $T$, hence the assertion is immediate.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), proof, printed p.197

proof.text: Now $S$ is integral. Apply generic open-image finiteness to obtain a nonempty open $S^\circ$ and a bound $b_0$. By open restriction, $G_q=R^qj_*F$ is constructible on $T^\circ=T\times_SS^\circ$ and is zero there for $q>b_0$. This generic input has no finite-type-over-a-field assumption. It applies to the original constant coefficient field $A$.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), proof, printed p.197

proof.text: The proper closed subset $E=S\setminus S^\circ$ contains no generic point. Each of its irreducible components is therefore a single closed point: a strict specialization inside such a component would, with the generic point of $S$, make a chain of length two, contrary to $\dim S\leq1$. There are finitely many such components, say $s_1,\ldots,s_r$. If $S$ has dimension zero, $E$ is empty. Otherwise each $\mathcal O_{S,s_a}$ is regular local of dimension one, hence a DVR. Put $S_a=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s_a}$ and form $j_a:V_a\hookrightarrow T_a$ by base change. The closed fibre of $T_a$ is exactly $T_{s_a}$, with the same residue field.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), proof, printed p.197

proof.text: For each $a$, let $p_a:T_a\to T$ and let $F_a$ be the inverse image of $F$. It is constructible: pull its finite stratification and its finite constant local trivializations back to $V_a$. The base map $S_a\to S$ is locally ind-etale: on an affine neighbourhood of $s_a$, localization is the filtered colimit of the localizations at elements outside its prime, each an open immersion. The same holds for $p_a$. For a geometric point $t$ of $T_a$, ind-etale strict-local invariance identifies $(T_a)_{(t)}$ with $T_{(p_at)}$. The two stalk formulas for $j_a$ and $j$ are thus the cohomology of the identical scheme $V\times_TT_{(p_at)}$ with the identical pulled-back sheaf. Their canonical restriction maps are isomorphisms. The forgetful comparison supplies these formulas for $A$-module higher direct images; the maps commute with the action of every scalar in $A$. Stalk conservativity therefore gives $p_a^{-1}G_q\cong R^qj_{a*}F_a$ for every $q$. Exact inverse image allows us to commute restriction with cohomology.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), local reduction, expanded using Stacks etale-cohomology.tex theorem-higher-direct-images and strict-local invariance

proof.text: Apply closed-fibre DVR finiteness to $j_a,F_a$; all its hypotheses hold since $\ell$ remains a unit and separated finite-type morphisms and open immersions retain their properties after base change. Using the preceding isomorphism and then pulling back to the closed fibre gives that $G_q|_{T_{s_a}}$ is constructible for every $q$, and zero there for $q>b_a$, for some $b_a\geq0$. Only this restriction is taken from the local input. No comparison with the direct image of $j_{s_a}$ is claimed.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), proof, printed p.197

proof.text: For fixed $q$, choose finite constructible locally closed stratifications trivializing $G_q$ on $T^\circ$ and each $T_{s_a}$. Regard these strata as subschemes of $T$ by composing their immersions with the open immersion $T^\circ\to T$ or the closed immersion $T_{s_a}\to T$. A locally closed subset of a locally closed subset is locally closed; in the Noetherian space $T$ each such subset is constructible. The finitely many stratifications are disjoint and cover $T$, and the same finite constant module trivializations still apply. This is precisely the defining stratification of a constructible $A_T$-module sheaf. Take $c_F=\max(\{0,b_0\}\cup\{b_a:1\leq a\leq r\})$. If $q>c_F$, every geometric stalk of $G_q$ lies either over $S^\circ$ or over one of the $s_a$, where the restriction is zero. Stalk conservativity gives $G_q=0$. Taking the maximum over the finitely many components from step 1 finishes the proof.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1(i), proof, printed p.197

The item statement is unchanged from the earlier unsplit copy, its sources cite no SGA, and its closure contains no via-ancestor (no cycle). The six steps follow ILO's route: generic open plus local DVR. Step 1 uses rem-pc-regular-normal to reduce to integral components, with open restriction. Step 3 shows every non-generic point is closed because dim<=1, so E is a finite set of closed points, each with a DVR local ring by lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr. Step 4 compares S_a->S with S by ind-Zariski localization: the invariance node gives (T_a)_(t)=T_(p_a t) over T, then the stalk formula, the forget comparison and conservativity give the isomorphism (the global base-change arrow is the standard adjunction map). Step 5 checks the hypotheses of the DVR node by base-change nodes; the closed fibre of T_a is T_{s_a}. Step 6 glues the strata, which is elementary in Noetherian T, and takes the maximum of finitely many bounds. The generic node is Deligne's generic finiteness over an integral Noetherian base, true and not a duplicate: thm-fin-deligne-generic-open and sk-thm-geo-generic-open need a base of finite type over a field, and the Gabber/quasi-excellent nodes need excellence. A later split of it must avoid SGA 4 1/2. The DVR closed-fibre node is true by ILO 2.3.1(i) or Zheng over Spec R, and strictly smaller than the item (local base, closed fibre only). A non-SGA split exists: completion plus Gabber-Fujiwara plus lem-per-quasi-excellent-etale-direct-image-finiteness. It is not a duplicate of the nearby-cycle or quasi-excellent nodes. The only other such node in the closure is lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change, a generic Mathlib leaf. The generic tool_uses are accepted.
